solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Senior politician engaged in celebratory drink, revealing significant place on board (7)

indicatorNotes.engaged in: someone engaged in a thing is taken up inside it

blocks.note: a toast is a drink raised to celebrate
PM = Prime Minister, placed inside TO…AST

annotation.surface: The Prime Minister joins a celebratory toast, letting slip news of an important boardroom seat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a company board; it means aboard a ship, where the topmast sits high up the mast.
annotation.definitionFit: A topmast is the section of mast above the lower mast on a sailing ship, a lofty and important place on board.

entries.clue: 50% take stock, abandoning core piece of work (4)

indicatorNotes.50%: fifty per cent is one half, so only half the letters of the next word survive
indicatorNotes.abandoning core: the word gives up its middle letters

annotation.surface: A half-hearted stocktake that skips the central part of the job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take stock' reads as one phrase; the clue splits it, halving the first word and hollowing the second.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a task is a job set to be done, a single piece of work.

entries.clue: Rare medicine is beginning to treat scientist (9)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: only the beginning of the next word is taken

blocks.note: physic is an old word for medicine, rarely used now

annotation.surface: A doctor turns to an unusual drug to treat a researcher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rare' is not about scarcity of the drug but about the word: physic survives mostly in older writing.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a physicist is one kind of scientist, working on matter and energy.

entries.clue: Precautionary intervention shortening operation? (1,6,2,4,5,4)

annotation.answer: A STITCH IN TIME SAVES NINE

blocks.note: the surface suggests a medical step taken early; the setter means any small timely repair
reads as cutting surgery short; meant as saving later work, nine stitches' worth

annotation.surface: A surgeon steps in early to cut an operation short.
annotation.walkthrough: The surgical picture fits literally: an early stitch spares a longer job later. The proverb means prompt small repairs prevent bigger ones.
annotation.definitionFit: The proverb recommends a timely small fix as a precaution, which shortens the work needed later.

entries.clue: Campaign elevated science after diplomacy (7)

annotation.definitionNote: Tactics is a plural noun for a plan of action; 'Campaign' stands for it as a noun.

indicatorNotes.elevated: in a down clue, raising a word writes it bottom to top
indicatorNotes.after: the science piece comes after the diplomacy, so it is sent second

blocks.note: SCI, short for science, turned upwards

annotation.surface: A political campaign puts science on a pedestal once the diplomatic work is done.
annotation.walkthrough: SCI is a standard short form of science, as in sci-fi.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose fit: tactics are the manoeuvres by which a campaign is fought, so the plan stands for the operation.

entries.clue: A TV screen offering new view of this author (9)

indicatorNotes.new view of: a new view presents the same letters in a different arrangement

annotation.surface: A television adaptation gives viewers a fresh look at a writer.
annotation.walkthrough: Miguel de Cervantes wrote Don Quixote, which has often been adapted for the screen.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by name: 'this author' points at the name spelled out by the letters, the Spanish author of Don Quixote.

entries.clue: Caught his teacher prancing about as Lewis Carroll character (8,3)

indicatorNotes.prancing about: the letters caper around into a new order

blocks.note: c = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation
ten letters to rearrange with the C

annotation.surface: A pupil catches his teacher clowning about dressed up as a character from Alice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like the verb of a pupil spotting the teacher; it is the single letter C.
annotation.definitionFit: The grinning Cheshire Cat appears in Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

entries.clue: More than one dissenting voice revokes comments implicating America (9)

indicatorNotes.implicating: to implicate is to fold something in, so America is wrapped inside

blocks.note: to recant is to take back what one said

annotation.surface: Someone withdraws remarks that dragged the United States into a scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: Recusants were historically those who refused to attend Church of England services, hence dissenters generally.
annotation.definitionFit: A recusant refuses to submit to authority, so several of them are dissenting voices.

entries.clue: A person at leisure to ignore one psychologist (5)

indicatorNotes.to ignore one: one is I, and ignoring it leaves it out

annotation.surface: Someone lounging about decides to take no notice of a therapist.
annotation.walkthrough: Alfred Adler was the Austrian founder of individual psychology and coined the 'inferiority complex'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Alfred Adler was a psychologist, a contemporary of Freud.

entries.clue: Wasted handwriting on editor unlikely to pay? (5-6)

blocks.note: one's fist is one's handwriting, an old usage

annotation.surface: A writer blames the editor for spoiling the manuscript, and doubts they'll be paid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' reads as squandered, but means drunk; 'fist' for handwriting is an old usage worth knowing.
annotation.definitionFit: A tight-fisted person is mean with money, so unlikely to pay up.

entries.clue: Second question posed by everyone in bad weather (6)

annotation.surface: Everyone asks a follow-up question about the storm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second question' reads as a follow-up query; it is two abbreviations side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: A squall is a sudden violent gust of wind, often with rain, so a burst of bad weather.

entries.clue: Difficult to lose heart in short walk (4)

indicatorNotes.to lose heart: the heart of a word is its middle letter, and it goes

blocks.note: a steep task is a hard one

annotation.surface: A hard stroll leaves the walker discouraged.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lose heart' reads as becoming discouraged; it means dropping the middle letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a place 'only a step away' is a very short walk off.

entries.clue: Commotion involving genetic material creating storm (7)

indicatorNotes.involving: to involve is to take something in

annotation.surface: A scandal over genetic engineering causes a media storm.
annotation.walkthrough: The storm in the surface is a media row; the answer is a real one.
annotation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, the fiercest kind of storm.

entries.clue: Some music and some food bit by bit (9)

blocks.note: a piece is a musical work
a meal is food eaten at one sitting

annotation.surface: A little music, a little food: an evening taken in small helpings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some' twice reads as a portion; each time it stands for one unit, a piece and a meal.
annotation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means done gradually, one bit at a time.

entries.clue: Futurist book article — chief source of surreal photomontages after editing (3,5,2,6,2,4)

annotation.answer: THE SHAPE OF THINGS TO COME

indicatorNotes.source of: a word's source is its first letter
indicatorNotes.after editing: the assembled letters are edited into a new order

blocks.note: thirteen letters, all rearranged with the rest

annotation.surface: A description of an avant-garde art book full of surreal photo collages.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chief source of surreal' reads as one phrase; only 'source of' is the first-letter instruction, and 'chief' goes in whole.
annotation.definitionFit: H. G. Wells's 1933 novel imagines the century ahead, so it is a book about the future.

entries.clue: The point of it is to prevent the loss of vital fluid (7,6)

annotation.definition: The point of it is to prevent the loss of vital fluid

blocks.note: reads as 'the purpose of it'; also the literal point of a pencil

blocks.clueFragment: is to prevent the loss of vital fluid
blocks.note: sounds grand, like saving a life; it is stopping blood from a shaving nick

annotation.surface: Someone explains the purpose of a device that stops blood loss.
annotation.walkthrough: A styptic pencil is a stick of astringent that stops bleeding from shaving nicks, applied by its tip.
annotation.definitionFit: Its whole purpose, applied by its tip, is to staunch small cuts and stop blood flowing.

entries.clue: Ineptitude of cowboy losing love by lake (9)

indicatorNotes.losing: the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: a gaucho is a South American cowboy
love = O, the zero score in tennis, dropped from GAUCHO

annotation.surface: A clumsy cowboy is jilted beside a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Losing love' paints a jilted cowboy; love is just the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: Gaucherie is social awkwardness or clumsiness, from French gauche.

entries.clue: Female is fine in legwear for engagements (10)

blocks.note: f = fine, as on pencil leads; placed inside T…IGHTS

annotation.surface: A woman looks fine in her tights for a round of social engagements.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Engagements' sounds like dates or betrothals; here it is the military sense, clashes.
annotation.definitionFit: An engagement is a fight, so fistfights are engagements fought bare-handed.

entries.clue: Alarms mostly uncovered dangerous reptile (11)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, all but its last letter

blocks.note: to rattle someone is to alarm them

annotation.surface: Alarms go off when a deadly snake is found almost out in the open.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Alarms' reads as a noun, warning bells; it is the verb, as in rattles someone.
annotation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is a venomous American pit viper, so a reptile to be feared.

entries.clue: Substantial source of hope around one religion (5)

indicatorNotes.source of: a word's source is its first letter
indicatorNotes.around: the first part goes around the next

blocks.note: fat = substantial, as in a fat cheque
one = I, the Roman numeral, placed inside FA…TH

annotation.surface: Religion as a great source of hope for everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Source of hope' sits comfortably beside religion in the surface, which hides that it gives only H.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in 'people of all faiths', meaning of all religions.

entries.clue: Puncture on corner taking out new truck (7)

blocks.note: a flat is a punctured tyre

annotation.surface: A truck gets a flat tyre going round a corner.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word fits a road accident, so the truck looks like part of the story rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A flatbed is a lorry with an open, flat loading platform.

entries.clue: Concentrated work from tailor is a speciality (6,4)

blocks.note: a strong solution is a concentrated one
a suit is what a tailor makes

annotation.surface: Focused tailoring is this craftsman's specialism.
annotation.walkthrough: A strong suit is originally a bridge term, the suit in which a player holds the most high cards.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: your strong suit is the thing you are best at.

entries.clue: Loose rocks landing on church — a harsh sound (7)

blocks.note: scree is loose broken rock on a slope

annotation.surface: A rockfall crashes onto a church roof with a terrible noise.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece landing on another sits above it, so the order is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: A screech is a harsh, piercing cry, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Persuade a Judge to tuck into cabbage (6)

indicatorNotes.to tuck into: the first pieces are tucked inside the next

blocks.note: cole is cabbage, as in coleslaw
j = judge; A and J go inside C…OLE

annotation.surface: Someone coaxes a judge into eating his greens.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tuck into' suggests eating, which fits the cabbage; here it means go inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to cajole is to persuade by coaxing and flattery rather than force.

entries.clue: Called up the whole amount on tucking into medicine (8)

indicatorNotes.tucking into: one piece is tucked inside another

blocks.note: used as written, placed inside M…ED

annotation.surface: A patient running up the total bill on medicines is phoned about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' reads as a preposition linking the pieces, but it is itself a piece.
annotation.definitionFit: To summon a witness or spirit is to call them up.

entries.clue: A universal constant capturing varying motion occurring spontaneously (9)

indicatorNotes.capturing: the outer letters take the next piece inside

blocks.note: c = the speed of light, a constant in physics

annotation.surface: A physicist describes a universal constant governing how things move of their own accord.
annotation.walkthrough: Autonomic describes bodily processes such as heartbeat that run without conscious control.
annotation.definitionFit: Autonomic functions happen involuntarily, of their own accord.

entries.clue: Master criminal, or one skewering victim? Not entirely (8)

indicatorNotes.skewering: to skewer is to run through, so the first piece sits inside the second
indicatorNotes.Not entirely: the word is not given in full; its last letter goes

blocks.note: MARTYR without its last letter; OR I goes inside M…ARTY

annotation.surface: A criminal mastermind or a killer stabbing a victim, only half described.
annotation.walkthrough: Professor Moriarty is Sherlock Holmes's arch-enemy, the Napoleon of crime.
annotation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle called Moriarty the master criminal behind half of London's crimes.

entries.clue: Bring back water sources containing river fish (5)

indicatorNotes.Bring back: the word is brought back, read from the end
indicatorNotes.containing: the result holds the next letter

blocks.note: taps supply water; turned round to SPAT

annotation.surface: An instruction to restore springs that hold river fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Water sources' suggests springs in the landscape; they are household taps.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a sprat is a small sea fish of the herring family.

entries.clue: Lute is redesigned, incorporating new instrument (7)

indicatorNotes.redesigned: the letters are given a new design
indicatorNotes.incorporating: the N is taken in with them

annotation.surface: A lute is remodelled into a new musical instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests music after the lute; here it is a tool, such as a kitchen implement.
annotation.definitionFit: A utensil is an instrument or implement, usually for the kitchen.

entries.clue: An American turned up, claiming a bath in Finland (5)

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters bottom to top
indicatorNotes.claiming: the result claims the next letter, holding it inside

blocks.note: US = American; AN US turned up gives SUNA

annotation.surface: An American tourist shows up and books a Finnish bath.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as arrived; in a down clue it means written upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: The sauna is the Finnish steam bath, and the word itself is Finnish.

entries.clue: Where potters try to make good breaks? (8,5)

annotation.definition: Where potters try to make good breaks?

blocks.note: suggests people who make pottery; meant as players who pot balls
reads as repairing breakages; a break is a run of scoring shots

annotation.surface: Where potters work at mending their broken pieces.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves carry a second sense from the game: potting balls, and a break as a scoring sequence.
annotation.definitionFit: Players pot balls and build breaks on a billiard table.

entries.clue: Succeeded in blocking actual revolving beam (5)

indicatorNotes.in blocking: the letter sits in the other word, blocking it
indicatorNotes.revolving: something revolving turns right round, so the word ends up back to front

annotation.surface: A revolving beam that actually stopped something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolving beam' pairs up naturally as a lighthouse light, but 'revolving' belongs with 'actual'.
annotation.definitionFit: A laser produces a narrow, intense beam of light, so it is named by what it emits.

entries.clue: Something to bore a daughter enthralled by fight (7)

indicatorNotes.enthralled by: held captive inside the next word

blocks.note: d = daughter; A D goes inside BR…AWL

annotation.surface: A tedious girl gets absorbed in watching a fight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Something to bore' suggests a dull person; it is a tool that bores holes.
annotation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small pointed tool for making holes in wood.

entries.clue: Shock call to start adopting metres (9)

indicatorNotes.adopting: the first word takes the letter into its family, inside it

blocks.note: to dub is to name or call
to found is to start up

annotation.surface: A startling phone call about taking up the metric system.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Call' reads as a phone call; it is the verb dub, to give a name.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to dumbfound is to shock someone so badly they are struck dumb.

entries.clue: Greek goddess put off accepting me (7)

indicatorNotes.accepting: the word takes the next one in

blocks.note: to deter is to put off

annotation.surface: A goddess is discouraged from taking the speaker in.
annotation.walkthrough: Demeter is the harvest goddess, mother of Persephone; the Romans called her Ceres.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Demeter is one of the Olympian goddesses of Greek myth.

entries.clue: Horrible couple keeping spades in bad condition (9)

indicatorNotes.keeping: the word keeps the letter inside it

blocks.note: s = spades, the card suit, placed inside DI…RE

annotation.surface: A nasty couple leave their gardening spades in a shocking state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Horrible couple' reads as two unpleasant people; the words split into two separate pieces, with the S kept by the first.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a building fallen into disrepair is in poor shape from neglect.

entries.clue: Exemplified here, in oboe’s part? (11)

indicatorNotes.in: one word sits in the other

blocks.note: the reed is the mouthpiece of an oboe

annotation.surface: A musician points to a passage in the oboe line as the example.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oboe’s part' suggests the music an oboist plays; it is a physical part of the instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: To represent something is to exemplify or stand for it.

entries.clue: Her stamina is transformed, absorbing fresh stimulus (1,4,2,3,3)

indicatorNotes.is transformed: the letters are transformed into a new order
indicatorNotes.absorbing: the result soaks up the next word inside

blocks.note: hot = fresh, as in hot news; placed inside AS…INTHEARM

annotation.surface: A woman's energy is transformed after she takes in a new stimulus.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like an anagram signal beside 'transformed'; it is the word HOT, as in hot off the press.
annotation.definitionFit: A shot in the arm is a boost, originally an injection, so a stimulus.

entries.clue: Mistakenly run a story covering an ancient creature (11)

indicatorNotes.Mistakenly: the letters are put down wrongly, in a new order
indicatorNotes.covering: the rearranged letters cover the next word

annotation.surface: A newspaper mistakenly publishes a piece about a fossil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run a story' is newspaper talk, which hides that it is the letters to be rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: The tyrannosaur was a huge meat-eating dinosaur of about 66 million years ago.

entries.clue: Dessert portion about reasonable? Not entirely (7)

indicatorNotes.about: the first word goes about the second
indicatorNotes.Not entirely: the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: FAIR without its last letter, placed inside PAR…T

annotation.surface: A diner questions whether the pudding serving is fair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dessert portion' reads as one phrase; the definition stops after 'Dessert'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a parfait is a rich frozen dessert, often layered in a glass.

entries.clue: Each year, benefit disrupted by mounting dispute and forms? (9)

indicatorNotes.disrupted by: the word is broken open by the next piece
indicatorNotes.mounting: in a down clue, mounting reads the word upwards

blocks.note: a perk is a benefit of a job
ROW, a dispute, written upwards; placed inside PER…K

annotation.surface: An annual benefits claim held up by a growing row over the forms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mounting' reads as growing; in a down clue it means the word climbs upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Forms are typical paperwork; the question mark flags that forms are only one example.

entries.clue: Performs piano melodies (5)

annotation.surface: A pianist performs tunes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piano' reads as the instrument; it is the musical direction for soft, abbreviated P.
annotation.definitionFit: To play is to perform, on stage or on an instrument.

entries.clue: Teams erase unexpected criticism (9)

blocks.note: to wipe a tape is to erase it

annotation.surface: Teams delete a surprise attack made on them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unexpected' could be taken as an anagram signal; it belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A sideswipe is a passing critical remark made when discussing something else.

entries.clue: Insect circling greyish horse without any point (9)

indicatorNotes.circling: the first word goes round the next

blocks.note: a dun is a greyish-brown horse, placed inside RE…DANT

annotation.surface: A fly buzzes round a grey horse, to no purpose.
annotation.walkthrough: The insect has to be a specific one, the two-word RED ANT, before it can wrap the horse.
annotation.definitionFit: Something redundant is superfluous, serving no point.

entries.clue: Greatly want to interrupt quiet comment nearby (9)

indicatorNotes.to interrupt: the word breaks into the middle of the next

blocks.note: an aside is a remark made quietly
to long is to want greatly, placed inside A…SIDE

annotation.surface: Someone badly wants to cut in on a remark whispered nearby.
annotation.walkthrough: An aside is a stage term: a remark an actor makes to the audience, unheard by the others.
annotation.definitionFit: Alongside means close beside, nearby.

entries.clue: Trimmed small mesh for basket (6)

indicatorNotes.Trimmed: the word is trimmed of its last letter

annotation.surface: A small trimmed piece of mesh is used to make a basket.
annotation.walkthrough: A punnet is the small square basket soft fruit such as strawberries is sold in, common in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: A punnet is a small basket or container for fruit.

entries.clue: Never angry over Charlie and I turning up, always on the move (7)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down clue, the pair is turned to read upwards

blocks.note: C for Charlie in the phonetic alphabet, then I; turned up to IC

annotation.surface: Someone never cross with Charlie and me, however much we keep moving around.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts NO MAD above the reversed pair.
annotation.definitionFit: Nomadic people wander from place to place, always on the move.

entries.clue: Source of alarm and commotion: Grandma dispensing a poison (10)

indicatorNotes.dispensing: to dispense with is to do without, so the named letter goes

annotation.surface: Grandma hands out poison, causing alarm and uproar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dispensing' makes Grandma a poisoner handing it out; it means doing without the letter A.
annotation.definitionFit: Belladonna is deadly nightshade, a poisonous plant, and the poison drawn from it.

entries.clue: A politician, bored, ousting leader to get excited (5,2)

indicatorNotes.ousting leader: the word throws out its first letter

annotation.surface: A tired politician gets thrown out as party leader, only to be fired up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ousting leader' reads as a party coup; it removes the first letter of FED UP.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang synonym: amped up comes from amplified, turned up to full volume, hence excited.

entries.clue: Purge Conservative breaking rank (5)

indicatorNotes.breaking: the letter breaks into the word

annotation.surface: A political purge as a Tory breaks ranks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rank' reads as a party's ranks; here it is the adjective, as in a rank smell.
annotation.definitionFit: Both mean clean out thoroughly; scouring purges a pipe or pan of what clogs it.

entries.clue: Armed guards? Parisian is suppressing startled comment (6)

annotation.definitionNote: Escort is a collective noun here: a body of armed guards.

indicatorNotes.is suppressing: to suppress is to hold down, so the comment is held inside

blocks.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise; placed inside ES…T

annotation.surface: A Parisian holds back a gasp at the sight of armed security.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cor!' is everyday British slang for 'wow' or 'gosh'.
annotation.definitionFit: An escort is a group of guards accompanying someone for protection.

entries.clue: Suggestive short skirts with contemporary jacket (11)

indicatorNotes.jacket: a jacket wraps around what it covers

blocks.note: minis are miniskirts; placed inside RE…CENT

annotation.surface: A racy outfit: miniskirts worn with a modern jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suggestive' hints at raciness in the surface; it means calling something to mind, as in reminiscent of.
annotation.definitionFit: Reminiscent means suggestive of something, evoking it.

entries.clue: Inclined to be bad-tempered, like an international match? (5)

blocks.note: a plain sense: quick to lose one's temper
an international cricket match is a Test, and -Y makes it 'Test-like'

annotation.surface: Tempers flare during a fiercely contested international game.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second sense as an invented word: a Test is an international cricket match, and adding Y makes an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Testy means irritable and quick to take offence; the second sense reads the word as Test plus Y.

entries.clue: Road maintenance vehicle currently parking in Berkshire town (10)

indicatorNotes.in: the pieces go in the town's name

blocks.note: Slough is a town in Berkshire, west of London
p = parking; NOW P goes inside S…LOUGH

annotation.surface: A council gritting lorry is now parked in a Berkshire town.
annotation.walkthrough: P for parking is the letter on British car-park signs.
annotation.definitionFit: A snowplough clears snow from roads, keeping them usable.

entries.clue: Turn to buy drinks, but not round in bar (4)

blocks.note: in British slang, it's my shout means it's my turn to buy the round
the round letter, taken out of SHOUT

annotation.surface: In a pub, someone dodges their turn to buy a round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Round' is the pub round in the surface; it is the round letter O. 'Bar' is the verb, not the pub.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: barring a door and shutting it both keep people out.

entries.clue: Party rejected, exhausted, not in office — not a regular thing (3,3,3)

indicatorNotes.rejected: the word is sent back, reversed

blocks.note: a party out of power is out

annotation.surface: A worn-out party voted out of government is now an irregular presence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party rejected' reads as a political party losing an election; the party is a DO, a social event.
annotation.definitionFit: The odd one out is the item that does not fit the regular pattern.

entries.clue: Cleaning up excavation in beach linked to European country (4,3,6)

indicatorNotes.in: one word goes in the other

blocks.note: a pit is a hole dug out; placed inside S…AND

annotation.surface: A dig on a beach is tied to a European country's clean-up campaign.
annotation.walkthrough: 'European country' gives the adjective POLISH rather than the noun Poland.
annotation.definitionFit: Spit and polish is thorough cleaning and smartening, as of soldiers' boots.

entries.clue: Become free of King Richard after beheading (4)

indicatorNotes.after beheading: the word loses its head, its first letter

blocks.note: DICK, short for Richard, without its D

annotation.surface: Kingdom freed when King Richard is executed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' reads as the order of the pieces; it belongs with 'beheading'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to kick a habit is to break free of it.

entries.clue: Some lingerie stand displaying children’s toy (5,4)

blocks.note: a teddy is a one-piece undergarment
to bear is to stand, tolerate

annotation.surface: A shop's lingerie stand features a cuddly toy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a display stand; it is the verb, as in 'can't stand it'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the stuffed bear is the classic soft toy of childhood.

entries.clue: Excuse you couldn’t make by SMS? (7)

annotation.definition: Excuse you couldn’t make by SMS?

blocks.note: the plain sense: a false reason put forward to cover the real one
the setter's joke: split the word so it seems to mean something from before text messages existed

annotation.surface: Someone muses on an excuse that can't be sent by text message.
annotation.walkthrough: Split as PRE-TEXT, the word seems to mean something that comes before texting, so it could not be sent by SMS.
annotation.definitionFit: A pretext is a false reason given to hide the real one, an excuse.
